transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because there’s this thing that’s been going on for a while, and I know it may sound strange when I say it out loud, but I’ve been having a really hard time shaking it.

I work as a financial advisor here in Cincinnati, and I’m around a lot of people in finance, and sometimes arts-related events too—fundraisers, panels, gallery things, networking events, that kind of circle. And over time I started feeling like certain people in those circles were paying attention to who I meet with, like which clients I’m seeing or talking to, and then sort of… sending signals about it. Not directly, not like someone comes up and says anything, but through things like invitations I get, or the topics they choose for panels, or even who ends up sitting near me at events.

I do try to tell myself, okay, maybe this is coincidence, maybe I’m connecting dots that aren’t there. But then something else happens and it feels too specific, and I can’t really let it go. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Can you think of a specific instance where you felt something was directed at you or related to you personally? If so, can you describe what happened?

Yeah. One that sticks with me was this panel event downtown—finance-adjacent, but with an arts nonprofit involved too. I had met with a client earlier that week, someone connected to a private foundation, and I hadn’t really mentioned that meeting to many people. Then I got invited to this event, and the topic was framed around “ethical stewardship” and “who influences community money,” which… I know, that could just be a normal topic in those circles, but it felt pointed.

And then when I got there, the seating felt strange. A couple people I recognize from the arts fundraising scene ended up right near me, and one of them made this passing comment about how “some advisors are more visible than they think.” It wasn’t said directly to me, exactly, but I heard it and I felt like it was meant for me. Like they were letting me know they knew who I’d been meeting with.

I remember sitting there trying to tell myself, okay, don’t overreact, this could be coincidence, people say vague things at panels all the time. But it lined up too neatly—the invitation, the topic, the people near me, that comment. I kept replaying it afterward, and it was hard to convince myself it wasn’t connected to me personally.

Do you believe that these signals or comments made by others have a special meaning specifically for you that other people wouldn't understand or recognize unless they were paying close attention to you too?

Yeah… I think that’s exactly what bothers me, honestly. It feels like there’s a layer to it that other people wouldn’t catch unless they knew the context of my client meetings or were watching the same patterns I’m watching.

Like, if someone else got the same invitation or heard the same panel topic, they’d probably just think, okay, normal Cincinnati arts-and-finance networking language. But for me it doesn’t land that way, because it lines up with who I’ve met with, or what conversations I’ve had, or who suddenly seems to be around me at these events. It feels like these little signals are meant to tell me, without saying it directly, that certain people know who I’m talking to and are tracking it somehow.

I do go back and forth in my head, like maybe I’m over-reading it, maybe it’s coincidence, maybe I’m just noticing things because I’m already worried about it. But then another invitation comes through, or a panel topic seems oddly close to something from my work, or someone sits near me who feels connected to that circle, and it’s hard for me to dismiss. It feels too specific to just shrug off. So yes, I guess I do believe there’s a special meaning there, even if I know most people wouldn’t see it unless they were paying very close attention.

Have you ever felt like these signals or messages are part of a larger hidden system or plan that only you can understand, something that goes beyond just people paying attention to your professional activities?

I don’t know if I’d call it a whole hidden system exactly… I mean, I don’t have some complete theory where everything fits together perfectly. But it does feel bigger than just one or two people noticing my schedule, if that makes sense.

It’s more like there are these connected circles here in Cincinnati—the finance people, the arts nonprofit people, the fundraisers, people who sit on boards or know clients with foundations—and I’ve started feeling like certain people in that world are quietly tracking who I meet with. Not openly, but in this sideways way. Like I’ll have a client meeting, and then an invitation shows up with a theme that feels uncomfortably close to that conversation, or I’ll go to an event and the panel topic seems to be hinting at the kind of client I’ve just seen, or someone ends up sitting near me who I associate with that same network.

And I know how that sounds. I really do. Part of me keeps saying, these are normal events, normal topics, people sit wherever, invitations go out to mailing lists. But then the timing or the wording feels too precise, and I can’t really let it go. It feels like they’re sending little signals to let me know they know who I’m talking to, even though they never say it directly.

So… not like I understand some grand plan that nobody else could ever see. But I do feel like there’s a pattern that most people wouldn’t notice, because they don’t know my client meetings or the sequence of things the way I do. And once I see that pattern, it’s hard to unsee it.
Have you ever felt that things unrelated to you—like things you see on TV, things people say in public, or events happening around you—have a special meaning or are directed at you personally?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of the main reason I came in, honestly. Not so much TV, necessarily, but things around me—public comments, event topics, invitations, seating arrangements—stuff that should be ordinary. I’ll get an invitation to some arts or finance panel here in Cincinnati, and the wording will feel like it’s referring to something I just discussed with a client. Or I’ll be at an event and someone I know from those nonprofit or fundraising circles ends up sitting nearby, and then there’ll be a comment that sounds general on the surface, but to me it feels like it’s aimed at me.

And I know, if someone else heard it, they might just think I’m making connections that aren’t there. I tell myself that too. Like, these are normal professional circles, people overlap, themes repeat, and not everything is about me. I do understand that. But it’s hard because it keeps happening in ways that feel too lined up with who I’ve met with or what I’ve been working on.

So yes, I have felt like unrelated things—or things that should be unrelated—have this special meaning for me. Like certain people in the arts and finance circles are quietly tracking which clients I meet with and then sending little signals through the things they say, the topics they choose, even where people sit near me. Even when I try to write it off as coincidence, I can’t really let it go.
Have you ever felt like random or ordinary events, like something happening on the street or a stranger’s conversation, were specifically directed at you or had a hidden meaning just for you?

Yeah… yes, I have. I mean, it’s not every random thing on the street, like I’m not saying every stranger walking by is part of it, but ordinary things have started to feel less ordinary to me.

The reason I came in is that, for a while now, I’ve been really stuck on this feeling that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly keeping track of which clients I meet with. And then I’ll notice these little things afterward—an invitation to a panel that uses wording that feels too close to a client conversation, or a topic at an event that seems to line up with something I just dealt with professionally, or someone sitting near me who feels connected to that whole network. On the surface, those are normal things. People send invitations, panels have broad themes, seating is random. I know that.

But when it happens in sequence, it feels like it’s directed at me. Like it’s not a direct message, exactly, but a signal. A way of saying, “We know who you’ve been meeting with,” without actually saying it out loud.

With strangers’ conversations, it’s more that if I hear something in public that overlaps with one of those themes, I’ll catch myself wondering if it’s connected somehow. I try to talk myself down and say, okay, this could just be coincidence, you’re noticing patterns because you’re anxious about it. But honestly, even when I tell myself that, I can’t really let it go. It still feels like there’s a hidden meaning there that’s meant for me specifically.
Have you ever felt that thoughts are being placed in your mind by others, or that your own thoughts are being broadcasted or shared with people around you?

No… I don’t think so. Not in that way.

I’ve never really felt like someone was putting thoughts into my head, like they weren’t mine to begin with. My thoughts feel like my own thoughts, even when I get caught up in them or start overanalyzing something. And I don’t think people can hear what I’m thinking or that my thoughts are being broadcast around me.

I guess sometimes I worry people know things they shouldn’t know, but that’s more about what they might have observed or pieced together, not like they’re literally inside my mind. If I’m sitting somewhere and I’m anxious, I might wonder what people are noticing about me, or whether I’m giving something away by my expression or the way I act. But that’s different from thinking my actual thoughts are being shared.

So, no, I haven’t noticed that. At least not the way you’re describing it.

Do you ever feel like completely ordinary things—like something written in a newspaper, a song playing in a store, or a random event on the street—are secretly about you or meant to communicate something to you specifically?

Yeah… I mean, yes, that’s basically what I’ve been trying to explain, though it’s not usually like a song in a store or a newspaper headline exactly. It’s more tied to the circles I’m in professionally here in Cincinnati—the arts events, finance people, nonprofit fundraising things, panels, invitations, that kind of world.

For a while now I’ve had this feeling—honestly more than a feeling, I get pretty convinced of it—that certain people in those arts and finance circles are keeping track of which clients I’m meeting with. Then afterward, something ordinary will happen, like I’ll get invited to a panel and the wording seems oddly close to a client issue I just discussed, or the topic of an event seems to echo something from work, or someone ends up seated near me who feels connected to the same group of people. And I know seating charts and event topics and invitations can all be normal. I really do know that, at least intellectually.

But when it lines up again and again, it feels like it’s meant to communicate something to me specifically. Not openly, not like someone saying, “We’re watching you,” but more like little signals. Like, “We know who you talked to,” or “We know what you’re involved in.” And then I’ll try to talk myself out of it and say maybe I’m just noticing patterns because I’m stressed or because these circles overlap, but it doesn’t really go away. I can’t fully let it go once it clicks into place in my head.

Have you ever had a sense that these signals or messages you’re noticing were being sent through unusual or supernatural means, like coded language, hidden technology, or something others wouldn’t be able to detect?

Not supernatural, no… I don’t think of it as, like, mystical or anything like that. And I’m not saying there’s some device hidden in the walls or some technology that only I can detect. It’s more ordinary than that, which almost makes it harder to explain without sounding ridiculous.

It feels like it’s happening through normal channels—emails, event invitations, panel descriptions, who gets seated where, who shows up at the same fundraiser or gallery thing. Like coded language, maybe, but not in a spy-movie way. More like people choosing wording carefully enough that it wouldn’t mean anything to anyone else, but to me it lands a certain way because of who I met with or what I was just involved in professionally.

So if an invitation comes through and the phrasing is really close to something from a client conversation, or a panel topic suddenly lines up with something I just dealt with, I start thinking, okay, that wasn’t random. That was meant as a signal. And then if the same names or the same circles keep appearing around it—the arts people, finance people here in Cincinnati, nonprofit event people—it starts to feel coordinated.

But no, I wouldn’t say supernatural. It’s more like… social signaling. Quiet tracking. People knowing which clients I’m meeting with and letting me know they know, but in a way that leaves them plausible deniability. And even when I tell myself, “This could just be coincidence, these circles overlap, you’re reading too much into it,” I can’t really drop it once I notice the pattern.
Do you feel certain that these signals are real and happening, even when others might tell you there's no evidence for them or try to reassure you it's just coincidence?

Yeah… that’s the part that’s hard, because I can say out loud that I don’t have, like, proof. I know someone else could look at the same invitation or the same panel topic or the same seating arrangement and say, “That’s just normal networking, that’s just Cincinnati being a small professional world, you’re connecting dots that don’t belong together.”

And I do try to tell myself that. I really do. I’ll literally sit there and go, okay, this could be coincidence, these arts and finance circles overlap, people invite the same people to the same things, maybe the wording only feels specific because I’m already thinking about that client or that issue. I can make the rational argument.

But then another thing happens, and it lines up again—an invitation comes in, or a topic gets announced, or someone is seated near me at an event—and it feels too pointed. Like it’s not just random. Like certain people know which clients I’ve been meeting with and they’re quietly letting me know they know. Not openly, but through these little signals.

So yes, I guess I do feel pretty convinced it’s real, even when people reassure me or when I try to reassure myself. I can doubt it for a little while, but I can’t really let it go once I’ve noticed the pattern.

But when it happens in sequence, it feels like it’s directed at me. Like it’s not a direct message, exactly, but a signal. A way of saying, “We know who you’ve been meeting with,” without actually saying it out loud.

With strangers’ conversations, it’s more that if I hear something in public that overlaps with one of those themes, I’ll catch myself wondering if it’s connected somehow. I try to talk myself down and say, okay, this could just be coincidence, you’re noticing patterns because you’re anxious about it. But honestly, even when I tell myself that, I can’t really let it go. It still feels like there’s a hidden meaning there that’s meant for me specifically.

No… I don’t think so. Not in that way.

I’ve never really felt like someone was putting thoughts into my head, like they weren’t mine to begin with. And I don’t think people can hear what I’m thinking or that my thoughts are being broadcast around me.

I guess sometimes I worry people know things they shouldn’t know, but that’s more about what they might have observed or pieced together, not like they’re literally inside my mind. If I’m sitting somewhere and I’m anxious, I might wonder what people are noticing about me, or whether I’m giving something away by my expression or the way I act. But that’s different from thinking my actual thoughts are being shared.

So, no, I haven’t noticed that. At least not the way you’re describing it.

Yeah… I mean, yes, that’s basically what I’ve been trying to explain, though it’s not usually like a song in a store or a newspaper headline exactly. It’s more tied to the circles I’m in professionally here in Cincinnati—the arts events, finance people, nonprofit fundraising things, panels, invitations, that kind of world.

Then afterward, something ordinary will happen, like I’ll get invited to a panel and the wording seems oddly close to a client issue I just discussed, or the topic of an event seems to echo something from work, or someone ends up seated near me who feels connected to the same group of people. And I know seating charts and event topics and invitations can all be normal. I really do know that, at least intellectually.

But when it lines up again and again, it feels like it’s meant to communicate something to me specifically. Not openly, not like someone saying, “We’re watching you,” but more like little signals. Like, “We know who you talked to,” or “We know what you’re involved in.” And then I’ll try to talk myself out of it and say maybe I’m just noticing patterns because I’m stressed or because these circles overlap, but it doesn’t really go away. patient.answer:
Not supernatural, no… I don’t think of it as, like, mystical or anything like that. And I’m not saying there’s some device hidden in the walls or some technology that only I can detect. It’s more ordinary than that, which almost makes it harder to explain without sounding ridiculous.

It feels like it’s happening through normal channels—emails, event invitations, panel descriptions, who gets seated where, who shows up at the same fundraiser or gallery thing. Like coded language, maybe, but not in a spy-movie way. More like people choosing wording carefully enough that it wouldn’t mean anything to anyone else, but to me it lands a certain way because of who I met with or what I was just involved in professionally.

So if an invitation comes through and the phrasing is really close to something from a client conversation, or a panel topic suddenly lines up with something I just dealt with, I start thinking, okay, that wasn’t random. That was meant as a signal. And then if the same names or the same circles keep appearing around it—the arts people, finance people here in Cincinnati, nonprofit event people—it starts to feel coordinated.

But no, I wouldn’t say supernatural. It’s more like… social signaling. Quiet tracking. People knowing which clients I’m meeting with and letting me know they know, but in a way that leaves them plausible deniability. And even when I tell myself, “This could just be coincidence, these circles overlap, you’re reading too much into it,” I can’t really drop it once I notice the pattern.

Yeah… that’s the part that’s hard, because I can say out loud that I don’t have, like, proof.
